key_insight: PhysAssistBench shows that medical LLMs must coordinate clinical knowledge, patient communication, and EHR tool use in the same conversation, and current models are not yet reliable at that combined task.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark suggests LLMs may be useful as physician assistants only if they can handle underspecified clinician requests, ambiguous patient replies, and precise record-system interactions together.
method: Built PhysAssistBench from real MIMIC-IV cases.
Created agentic patients that convert static EHR records into multi-turn clinical interactions while preserving factuality.
Added a curated bilingual, physician-validated evaluation set for interactive doctor-patient-EHR tasks.
evidence_signal: The benchmark includes 1,296 manually reviewed and physician-validated turns, and experiments found leading LLMs remain unreliable in this setting.
watch_item: Because the benchmark is based on simulated agentic patients, real-world deployment still needs careful validation for safety, robustness, and workflow fit.
paper_title: Are LLMs Ready to Assist Physicians? PhysAssistBench for Interactive Doctor-Patient-EHR Assistance
